chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayyna, from al-Ahwal who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I come out of the toilet, then I clean myself with water, and my garment falls into that water which I had cleaned myself with.' So he said: 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.استنجى: Istinja — the act of cleaning oneself after using the toilet, typically with water
key_terms.الخلاء: The toilet, privy — place of relieving oneself
key_terms.لا بأس: There is no harm/problem — a standard jurisprudential expression indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Does water used for istinja make clothing ritually impure if the garment falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a question about ritual purity (tahara) posed by al-Ahwal to Imam al-Sadiq (AS). The questioner asks whether a garment that comes into contact with water used for post-toilet cleaning (istinja) becomes ritually impure. The Imam rules that there is no harm in this, indicating that such used water does not transfer ritual impurity to the garment. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that water used for istinja, while no longer considered pure water, does not render objects it touches as najis (ritually impure) when certain conditions are met.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Al Ahowl who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I come out of the toilet, then I clean myself with the water. So, something from that water hits my clothes which I have cleaned myself with’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ’Udhaynah from al-Ahwal who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I may use the toilet and then wash to clean myself but my clothes touch the water which was used for cleaning. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
